## Overwritten property This property is overwritten by another property in the same object literal. ---

In general, the solution is to remove or resolve the duplicate property so that the object literal has only one entry per key. The most robust way, if the two 'Moonlight Silver' color codes are supposed to be the same, is to remove one of the entries. If they're different, or should be brand-specific, the data structure should be reworked to support that.

Given the constraints (only work with shown code), and assuming both entries assign the same color code ('#C0C0C0'), we should remove one. In the provided snippet, line 69 defines 'Moonlight Silver': '#C0C0C0' under Tecno. Since a later 'Moonlight Silver' likely exists for Oppo, as hinted on line 32: 'Oppo': ['Starry Black', 'Moonlight Silver', ...], the probable best solution (for minimal disruption) is to remove the occurrence in the Tecno color block at line 69, leaving the later definition for Oppo to remain.

If in fact the newer, later value is more accurate for Oppo, keeping that is correct because JavaScript object literal semantics always prefer the "last" one. This will also eliminate the CodeQL warning.
